text:
Every lesson has a design section.

This is where you'll start designing a solution to a problem. It probably won't be perfect, but each lesson you'll make improvements. That's how engineers do it - piece by piece!

tiles.title: Who will your team design for?

text: Read about the different people below, and choose one person who your team will design a specialized bionic arm for.

tiles.title: The people you can design for are on a handout!
What motion do you want to start with?

text:
An important part of engineering is iteration: trying things and improving it over time. You can probably think of a LOT of different motions and functions that would be useful for your person. Over time, you will make prototypes with more features, but you probably won’t figure it out all at once.

One way to start is to focus on something very specific.

What is one motion or action that you think is especially important for this person? Why did you choose to start with that motion?

tiles.title: Write the name of the person you picked here!

text: You can try writing: [Person's name] needs to be able to [make this motion]. This is a good motion to start with for them because _______________.

Here are a few designs for an initial prototype (the instructions are in handouts).

None of them is perfect. We added a few pros and cons for each one.

Decide which one your team will make, but also think about one improvement you can make to it that will be helpful for the person you chose.

It can be a big or small change, but it should be feasible - meaning, you should be able to actually make that improvement!

The students are likely to come up with different improvements than they initially designed. If you want, you can get them to start making the prototype and just describe their improvements at the end.

How will you improve your prototype? You can...

1. Write your ideas

2. Sketch your ideas using the sketch tile

3. Draw your ideas on paper and take a picture
